annotation.title_clean: Compliance with Safety Assurance in Robotic Surgery: An Analytical Study in the Light of Jordanian Medical and Health Liability Law No. (25) of the Year 2018
annotation.title_en: Compliance with Safety Assurance in Robotic Surgery: An Analytical Study in the Light of Jordanian Medical and Health Liability Law No. (25) of the Year 2018
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Adaileh, A.T.; Al-Araishy, O.A.; Al Hawamdeh, M.H.
annotation.venue: Global Journal of Politics and Law Research
annotation.summary_en: Legal doctrinal study of the surgeon's obligation to ensure patient safety in robotic surgery under Jordan's Medical and Health Liability Law No. 25 of 2018. It finds the law silent on this duty and recommends mandatory surgeon training on surgical robots and an explicit statutory duty to inform patients.
key_provisions_or_claims: Jordan's Law No. 25 of 2018 does not explicitly state the physician's duty to ensure patient safety.
Safety assurance involves anticipating adverse events and taking measures to prevent or mitigate them.
Physician's duty regarding equipment-related safety (e.g., sterilization, training) is one of achieving a result.
Recommends mandatory explicit training for surgeons operating surgical robots.
Recommends the duty to inform patients of robotic surgery risks be written into the law.
